localChanges: Late in a large game, computer players' turns are now about a fifth quicker again (#308).

log: `getByPlayer` scanned every city on each call. A city's owner changes when it's captured, so `City#capture` calls core-registry's `keysChanged(this)` before processing `Captured` (whose rules may look the city up by its new owner), and `CityRegistry` keeps the index up to date. Lookups answer as the scan did, in registration order, however often a city has changed hands. Destroyed cities are still left out unless asked for. Needs core-registry ^0.1.6 (civ-clone/web-renderer#308).

From review: the other capture test only looked after `capture` returned, so it would still pass with `keysChanged` moved after the rules. This one records the lookups from inside a `Captured` rule, and fails if it is.

An entry filed by something that can change (a unit's tile, a city's owner) calls `keysChanged(this)` from `@civ-clone/core-registry/keysChanged`, and every registry holding it re-files it. `EntityRegistry` asks to be told for each entry while it holds it, once it has an index. Watchers are held weakly both ways: by entry in a `WeakMap`, and each registry through a `WeakRef` (reached via `globalThis`, so it compiles against an ES2019/ES2020 `lib`; strong where there's no `WeakRef`). A registry dropped without unregistering its entries is not kept alive by them.
remembers the key each entry was filed under, so it can take the entry out of that bucket after its key has changed (no more scanning every bucket);

keeps each bucket in registration order, the order of `entries()`, so a lookup answers in the same order as the scan it replaces however often an entry has moved. Previously a re-filed entry went to the end. For keys that never change, nothing is different;
finds an entry in its bucket by binary search on that order;
has `refile(entity)`, which touches only a bucket whose key changed.
`reindex(entity)` is `keysChanged(entity)`: the same re-file, now without a search. `includes` reads the order map rather than scanning.

From review. `refile` compared the filed and current keys with `===`, but `Map` matches keys with SameValueZero, under which `NaN` is the same key as `NaN`. An unchanged `NaN` key was taken out and put back, which moves the entry to the end of its bucket in a standalone `RegistryIndex` (one without a registration order). The keys are now compared as the `Map` does. The regression test fails with `===`.

From review. A registry collected without unregistering left its `WeakRef` in each entry's watcher set until that entry's keys changed or it was unwatched. So an entry that outlived many registries without ever changing key collected one dead reference per registry. The registries themselves were freed; only the small wrappers stayed. `watchKeys` already walks the set, so it now drops cleared references as it goes.
`getByTile`, `getByCity` and `getByPlayer` scanned every unit on each call. On a turn-247 save (huge map, ~1,000 units) they were ~17% of a turn between them.

A unit's tile, city and owner change, so `Unit`'s three setters (`setTile`, `setCity`, `transfer`) now call `keysChanged(this)`, and `UnitRegistry` asks to be told (`lib/keysChanged`, a `WeakMap` from unit to the registries holding it, so nothing outlives the unit) while a unit is registered with it. `transfer` says so before processing `Transferred`, whose rules may look the unit up.

Lookups give exactly what the scan gave, in the same order. Each bucket is kept in registration order, which is the order of `entries()`. Destroyed units are still left out at lookup. Keys are compared as they are, so `null` and `undefined` cities stay apart as they did under `===`. Units restored from a save are filed when `hydrate` registers them, after their fields are filled.
Tested by a seeded 2,000-step fuzz against the old scan, and in web-renderer: conformance is identical, all save/load/isolation suites pass, and turns are 15–22% shorter (civ-clone/web-renderer#308).

From review. A move re-filed the unit under its owner and home city too, which hadn't changed. Removal was a linear search and both steps shift the bucket, so a move cost work in proportion to everyone sharing those keys; the bucket of units with no home holds units from every player. Now only buckets whose key changed are touched, and a unit is found in its bucket by binary search on its registration order. 20,000 moves of one unit among 5,000 sharing an owner and no home: 275 ms to 10 ms.

Each unit's watchers were held strongly, so a registry dropped without unregistering its units stayed reachable through them. They're held by `WeakRef` now, reached through `globalThis` so it compiles against the renderer's ES2020 `lib`, with a strong reference as the fallback where there's no `WeakRef`. A test checks that a dropped registry is collected; it needs `--expose-gc` and skips without it. Run with it, it fails with strong references and passes with weak ones.

The mechanism moved to core-registry 0.1.6, where `CityRegistry` (a city's owner changes on capture) and others can share it. `UnitRegistry` is now three `this.index(...)` declarations, and `Unit`'s setters call core-registry's `keysChanged`. Home cities of `null` and `undefined` are keyed by stand-in symbols, since the index leaves those keys out but the scan compared them with `===`. `lib/keysChanged` is removed before it was ever published.
